title: Optional Go WASM build for live matches
lead: Optional: build the arena for the browser with Go's stock `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm` target (C28) so a page can run live matches with the identical core, and show that it gives the native result and replay hash. v1 acceptance does not need this; the replay-only web viewer (S15) needs no WASM.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** web viewer UI or integrating live matches into it (S15 or later); any wasm toolchain beyond the Go distribution (wasm-pack, TinyGo, wasm-opt need owner approval, C13); committing `wasm_exec.js` or the `.wasm` binary.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Milestone 7 and C28: live in-browser matches, if wanted, use Go's stock js/wasm build (about 2 MB; `wasm_exec.js` ships with Go), so no extra toolchain is needed. Keeping it a separate optional slice keeps the web viewer replay-only and v1 acceptance (S17) independent of it.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `cmd/pitwasm/match.go` (no build tag): `runMatch(a, b []byte, seed uint64) (result []byte, replay []byte, hash string, err error)` over `internal/asm`, `internal/arena` and `internal/replay`.
- `cmd/pitwasm/match_test.go`: native test of `runMatch`.
- `cmd/pitwasm/main_js.go` (`//go:build js && wasm`): registers a `pitRun` function with `syscall/js` and blocks.
- `scripts/build-wasm.sh` (new): with `scripts/env.sh` sourced, runs `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build -o build/pit.wasm ./cmd/pitwasm` and copies `wasm_exec.js` from the Go installation into `build/` (in Go 1.24 and later it lives under `$(go env GOROOT)/lib/wasm/`; the implementer verifies the path for go1.27.2).
- `web/live.html`, `web/js/live.js`: load two bot sources and a seed, call `pitRun`, show the result and replay hash. Served with the local static server from S15 (extended to serve `build/` if needed).
- `AGENTS.md`: the WASM build command.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestRunMatchGolden` (native): `runMatch` on `bots/imp.s` vs `bots/dwarf.s` at seed 1 returns the replay hash pinned in S11.
- Under WASM (see Check): the page shows the same result text and hash.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
- Keep the binding thin; no game logic in `cmd/pitwasm` beyond calling the packages.
- `cmd/pitwasm/main_js.go` is the only file that imports `syscall/js`; `go vet ./...` on the host must still pass.
- Record the measured `build/pit.wasm` size in the note on this item.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `. scripts/env.sh && go test ./... && go vet ./... && test -z "$(gofmt -l cmd internal)"` passes.
- `. scripts/env.sh && sh scripts/build-wasm.sh` produces `build/pit.wasm` and `build/wasm_exec.js`; `git status --short` shows neither.
- Manual: serve the page, run imp vs dwarf at seed 1, and confirm the result and hash equal the native `pit run` output.
- Owner input, optional: an automated WASM run needs a JS host (Node, already installed here, via Go's `go_js_wasm_exec`). Node is a toolchain under C13, so it needs owner approval; without it, the manual check stands.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Branch `slice/<id>-wasm` in `.worktrees/<id>`. One commit when the owner asks.
